This model's own unit price is not on file, so the figure is the provider-level one and this model's real allowance may be lower. Binding limit: Neurons per day, at 10,000. On a small text model that is roughly a quarter of a million output tokens; on a large one, far fewer. Applies per ACCOUNT.

unranked.volume_evidence: Cloudflare bills in Neurons, not tokens, and publishes both the free allocation and the conversion on the same page. 10,000 Neurons a day divided by 34,868 Neurons per million output tokens is about 286,795 output tokens a day on llama-3.1-8b: their two numbers, our division, so it is marked DERIVED and never counted as measured. Where the tracked model's own Neuron price is in `neuron_cost_examples`, rank.py derives that model's figure from it instead; llama-3.3-70b costs six times more per output token than the 8b model. Seven models are excluded from the free tier entirely and need a paid billing method. 10,000 Neurons/day / 34,868 Neurons per 1M output tokens, @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8-fast. This model's own unit price is not on file, so the figure is the provider-level one and this model's real allowance may be lower. Binding limit: Neurons per day, at 10,000. On a small text model that is roughly a quarter of a million output tokens; on a large one, far fewer. Applies per ACCOUNT.
unranked.why_unranked: no official benchmark score published for this model

unranked.volume_evidence: Three tiers by account status. A new account is Solo: 50 free-model requests a day and 5 a minute. A top-up of Rp 10,000 moves it to Payer, at 1,000 a day. The header measured on 2026-09-07 read x-ratelimit-limit 5, which matches the Solo per-minute figure. 50 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 25,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. Binding limit: Fifty free requests a day until a top-up moves the account to Payer. Applies per ACCOUNT.

unranked.volume_evidence: Their pricing page answers what the header readings could not: the Free plan grants $10 a month in API credits. That is why the ceiling read 625,000 tokens a minute once and zero six times within an hour: a monthly pot, not a standing rate. A header limit of zero means the monthly pot is empty for the rest of the month, not that the tier is off. No token figure is published, so none is recorded here; the credit is in `monthly`. Binding limit: Ten dollars a month of credits, and no published conversion into tokens. Applies per ACCOUNT. VOLATILE: this figure moved under us at least once.

Free-tier values are not published; check your own console at /settings/limits. Every list that reprints 1,000 requests/day as a free-tier figure is reprinting a paid plan's number. 200,000 tokens/day is the provider's own token figure (DECLARED). This figure is the provider's Developer plan, not its free tier: it is shown and it is not ranked or summed. Binding limit: TPM, not RPD. 8,000 tokens per minute is what you actually hit: a long prompt returns 413 long before you approach 1,000 requests. We measured that 413 on an article-length prompt. Applies per ORGANIZATION.
